match.reason: No bank point teaches the regional case of water scarcity in West Asia and North Africa, including shared rivers and tension between nations; the closest cards cover general scarcity types and management methods for Australian courses.

draft.title: Water scarcity in West Asia and North Africa
card: West Asia and North Africa is the most water-scarce region in the world. Much of it is hot and dry, with little rainfall.
Many countries use desalination, which removes salt from seawater to make fresh water. It needs a lot of energy and money.
Some countries pump ancient groundwater, which is water stored underground for thousands of years. It is not refilled quickly, so it can run low if overused.
Rivers such as the Nile and the Tigris and Euphrates flow through more than one country. Nations share them, and this can cause tension over who uses how much.
draft.remember: Dry lands rely on desalination, old groundwater and shared rivers, which can cause tension.

a.q: Why can shared rivers such as the Nile cause tension between nations?
opts: Several countries depend on the same limited water
Rivers in this region contain too much salt
Each country owns the whole river it uses
Rivers flow only through one country at a time
a.why: A river that flows through more than one country must be shared, so one country's use can leave less for others. The Nile and the Tigris and Euphrates both cross borders, so the other options are wrong.
a.clue: Think about who else uses the water.

b.q: A country in this region has almost no rivers but a long coastline. It builds plants that make fresh water from the sea. What is a main drawback of this choice?
opts: It needs a lot of energy and money
It slowly drains ancient groundwater
It reduces the flow of shared rivers
It depends on regular heavy rainfall
b.why: Desalination removes salt from seawater, which takes large amounts of energy and money. It does not draw on groundwater or rivers, and it does not need rain, so those options are wrong.
b.clue: Think about what it costs to take salt out of seawater.

a.best: Several countries depend on the same limited water

b.best: It needs a lot of energy and money

problems.detail: The clue "Think about what it costs to take salt out of seawater" points straight at the answer "It needs a lot of energy and money", so a student can pick it without knowing the idea.
